# 1\. Executive Summary

This document defines Module 10 - System Information & Administration for iPOMS. It consolidates the complete business discussion - the original question of whether this module was even needed, the business justification, and the final decisions - into a single functional specification.

Module 10 is a compact management dashboard, not a technical server-administration console. Its purpose is to give the Director and CEO confidence that the application is healthy and a small number of organization-wide controls, without requiring them to open Firebase, ask a developer, or interpret technical metrics.

# 2\. Purpose - Why Module 10 Is Needed

Before this module was added, the explicit question was asked: do we really need it, and how does it help now and in future versions?

The original assumption - a traditional System Administration module with server monitoring, CPU usage, memory graphs, and logs - was rejected. Infoziant runs one organization, one CEO, one Director, one Team Leader, and roughly 20-25 users, with no customer-facing SaaS platform and no IT department monitoring servers all day. A complex administration console would likely never be used.

Instead, Module 10 gives management confidence that the application is healthy and a handful of organization-wide business controls - not technical controls. The guiding scenario: when the CEO logs in on a Monday morning, they should see Application Status, Users Online, Companies, Today's Logins, Database status, and Version at a glance, instead of opening Firebase or asking the developer.

# 3\. Module Scope - What Module 10 Is Not

Module 10 is deliberately kept small: not another operational module, not another tracker, and not a technical infrastructure console. No CPU usage, no RAM graphs, no server logs - the CEO does not need that level of technical detail.

Its long-term value grows with the organization: if Infoziant scales from roughly 20 coordinators to 100 coordinators, 300 colleges, and 40,000 companies, this module lets management see user growth, database growth, and application usage at a glance, without asking developers.

Almost all information shown is calculated from existing records (a count of user or company documents) rather than separately stored, so the module consumes negligible additional backend storage regardless of which database platform is ultimately chosen.

# 4\. Module Access

| **Role**              | **Access**           |
| --------------------- | -------------------- |
| Placement Coordinator | No access            |
| Team Leader           | View only (optional) |
| Director              | Full access          |
| CEO                   | Full access          |

Normal coordinators and, by default, team leaders never need to use this module - it exists for the Director and CEO.

# 5\. Section 1 - System Health

The first thing the Director or CEO sees. Shown as simple status indicators, not technical graphs:

- Application - Online / Offline
- Database - Connected / Disconnected
- Storage - Available / Unavailable
- Last Synchronization - date and time

Deliberately excluded: CPU usage, RAM usage, or any server performance graph - this level of detail is not useful to a non-technical business audience.

# 6\. Section 2 - Organization Snapshot

Described as the heart of Module 10 - a single glance that replaces multiple page visits. Shown together:

- Coordinators (total)
- Active Today
- Partial Working
- On Leave
- Blocked
- Deactivated
- Total Colleges
- Companies
- HR Contacts

# 7\. Section 3 - Database Growth

Presented as KPI cards rather than tables, matching the style used across other iPOMS dashboards (Module 07):

- Companies
- HR Contacts
- Reports (generated)
- Images

# 8\. Section 4 - Data Quality Monitor

One of the most valued additions in this module's design. Rather than simply reporting "everything is okay", it reports measurable data quality against the organization's biggest asset - its metadata database:

- Metadata Quality - an overall percentage score (e.g. 92%)
- Duplicate Companies
- Missing Email addresses
- Missing Mobile numbers
- Companies Without an assigned HR contact

This gives the Director a clear, immediate signal of where metadata quality needs attention, since a decline in metadata quality affects every downstream module (Daily Tracker, Daily Leads, Reports).

# 9\. Section 5 - Storage Summary

A compact, informational summary of overall system size and output, useful for the Director to understand growth over time and anticipate when infrastructure upgrades might be needed:

- Database Size
- Documents (count)
- Images (count)
- Reports Generated (count)

# 10\. Section 6 - Version Information

- Current Version
- Environment (e.g. Production)
- Release Date / Last Update
- Developer (Infoziant)

Simple, display-only information, useful during support conversations.

# 11\. Section 7 - Announcement Management

The System Announcement Banner was introduced in Module 09 (Settings & Configuration); Module 10 is where the Director or CEO operationally creates and manages it, as a compact panel rather than a pop-up:

- Title
- Message
- Start Date
- End Date
- Publish action

Every logged-in user sees a published announcement until it expires or is removed - useful for planned maintenance, policy updates, or organization-wide messages without sending separate emails or WhatsApp messages.

# 12\. Section 8 - Maintenance Mode

Presented as a simple on/off switch rather than a complex configuration screen:

- Maintenance Mode - On / Off toggle
- Affected Users - which roles are shown the maintenance screen (Coordinators, Team Leaders, Director, CEO - configurable per role)
- Reason - free text, shown to affected users
- Start Time / End Time

Business rule: Coordinators should never be shown raw application errors caused by planned system work. When Maintenance Mode is on, affected users instead see a professional "System Under Maintenance" screen stating the expected completion time, rather than an error page.

# 13\. Overall Status Banner

An enterprise-level addition placed at the very top of the module: a single, prominent, colour-coded status strip that communicates overall condition before any detailed metric is read.

| **Status**                 | **Example**                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Healthy (green)            | "System Healthy - No Issues Detected - Last Checked Today 09:45 AM" |
| Attention Required (amber) | "12 Duplicate Companies Found - Review Recommended"                 |
| Action Required (red)      | "Database Connection Lost - Please Contact Administrator"           |

The CEO does not need to interpret dozens of metrics individually - the banner communicates overall condition immediately, with the detailed sections below available for deeper investigation when needed.

# 14\. Screen Layout

Module 10 is designed to fit on a single page with clearly divided sections and almost no scrolling - Status Banner, then System Health / Organization Snapshot / Storage / Version at a glance, then Database Statistics, then the Data Quality Monitor, then Announcement and Maintenance Mode panels side by side.

Design intent, stated directly: within the first 5 seconds the Director or CEO should know whether everything is healthy; within the next 10 seconds, what (if anything) needs their attention; and if something needs action, they click directly into the relevant section to manage it. This mirrors the design philosophy followed since Module 1 - keep day-to-day operations simple while giving management the right level of visibility.

# 15\. Business Rules Summary

- Module 10 is intentionally small - a management dashboard, not a technical server-administration console, and not another operational module or tracker.
- No CPU, RAM, or server performance graphs are shown anywhere in this module.
- Coordinators have no access; Team Leader access is view-only and optional; Director and CEO have full access.
- Almost all displayed figures are calculated counts of existing records rather than separately stored data, keeping backend storage cost negligible.
- The Data Quality Monitor reports against the metadata database specifically, since metadata quality directly affects every other operational module.
- Announcement publishing is operationally owned by Module 10, while the resulting banner is displayed to users as defined in Module 09.
- Maintenance Mode always shows affected users a professional maintenance screen with an expected completion time - never a raw system error.
- A single colour-coded status banner (green / amber / red) always sits above the detailed sections so overall health can be read in seconds.

# 16\. Deferred / Out of Scope for v1.0

- Server-level technical monitoring: CPU usage, RAM usage, request logs, or infrastructure-level performance graphs.
- Any database platform decision (Firebase vs. MongoDB vs. another option) - explicitly deferred and not to influence this module's design.
- Automated alerting or paging beyond the on-screen status banner.
- Team Leader access is optional and may be enabled or left disabled depending on organizational preference at implementation time.

# 17\. Conclusion

Module 10 is considered functionally complete for Version 1.0. Despite being the smallest module in iPOMS, System Information & Administration gives the Director and CEO a fast, non-technical view of system health, organization snapshot, database growth, data quality, and organization-wide controls (announcements, maintenance mode) - reinforcing the same philosophy applied across every other module: keep daily operations simple while giving management the right level of visibility.

# 18\. Next Module

With Modules 1-10 now functionally complete, business-level design planning is essentially finished. The next stage is system-level planning before implementation: the iPOMS UI Design Foundation (Visual Identity and the Enterprise Component Library, already frozen), followed by the Screen Blueprint System and Technical Architecture chapters that translate this business design into buildable pages and a development-ready technical specification.
